messages:
incident-bot: Pager: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Current p99=3.8s (SLO breach). Affected customers: 8 high-volume API keys. Paging @alex oncall :rotating_light:

alex: I got the page, jumping in. Any quick metrics? p95/p99 and streaming stall counts?

sam: tl;dr — we pushed a runtime change ~14:20 UTC, since then prefix cache hit rate dropped massively. p95 ~350ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~600ms -> 3.8s, streaming stalls up x6.

maria: can you post the cache hit-rate graph and recent deploy id?

sam: hit rate (prefix cache): pre-deploy 0.89 -> post-deploy 0.06. Deploy id: runtime-deploy-20260314-98f3. Logs show many cache misses and subsequent heavy KV recompute.

sam: posting quick snippet from logs:
```
2026-03-14T14:22:11Z INFO cache miss key=prefix_v2:8c9a1f... compute KV 0.120s
2026-03-14T14:22:11Z INFO cache miss key=prefix_v2:4b3f2d... compute KV 0.118s
2026-03-14T14:22:11Z WARN streaming stall session=abc123 stall_ms=3200
```

ira: any code change that could explain key churn?

sam: yes — PR #4128 changed key format. Old: `cache_key = f"prefix:{md5(prefix)}"` New: `cache_key = f"prefix_v2:{sha1(prefix)}"` (intended for future-proofing). Migration not executed, so old keys and new keys don't overlap -> cold cache for everything.

jordan: ohhh. so massive cold traffic hitting model runtime and recomputing KV per-request, explains p99 tail.

maria: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback the deploy, 2) enable compatibility layer to look up both key formats, 3) temporarily widen autoscaling / reserve capacity to handle recompute while we fix.

alex: priority order: 1) rollback to restore SLOs, 2) enable compatibility in a followup non-breaking change if rollback is risky, 3) rewarm cache. Agreed?

sam: agree. rollback is fastest. Rolling back now. deploy-bot: initiating rollback to runtime-deploy-20260314-73b2 (previous stable).

deploy-bot: rollback started -> pods terminating 3/12 -> new pods 12/12 ready.

sam: after rollback metrics (next 3 min): prefix cache hit rate back up to 0.78, p95 dropped to ~320ms, p99 dropped to 620ms and trending down. Streaming stall counts decreasing.

alex: good. Can we confirm any customers still impacted? Ira, can you coordinate customer notifications?

ira: reached out to top-3 affected customers via email + in-product banner. One customer reported degraded streaming during the window (14:20-14:35 UTC). We asked for logs and offered mitigation steps. CS notified.

maria: post-rollback followups we need before green:
- add CI check that flags key-schema changes (diffs in cache key functions)
- add canary test exercising heavy prefix cache warmup during deploys
- add compatibility fallback in runtime (read both key variants for N minutes)
- infra task: implement a migration tool to rekey existing cache entries safely
- update runbook with clear rollback threshold (cache-hit < 0.2 AND p99>2s)

sam: re: rekeying — we can run a rewriter job: iterate old keys -> compute v2 key -> copy TTL. Quick proof-of-concept on staging: `redis-cli --scan --pattern "prefix:*" | while read k; do v2=$(echo $k | sed 's/^prefix:/prefix_v2:/'); ttl=$(redis-cli ttl $k); redis-cli get $k | redis-cli set $v2 - ex $ttl; done`

jordan: careful: copying at scale will spike Redis IO. We should throttle and do in batches, monitor redis_cpu. Option: run in k8s job with rate limit.

alex: agreed. Sam, plan the rekey job with throttling and monitoring. Maria, add to postmortem the required CI and runbook changes. Ira, continue customer comms with timelines. I'll take ownership of postmortem.

sam: action: open PR to add compatibility read-path that checks v2 then v1 for 10m after deploy and a feature flag. Also creating rekey job proposal (batch size 500 keys/s, pause 200ms between batches).

maria: also add an alert: sudden drop in cache hit rate >30% AND p99 increase >1s should page oncall immediately (we had alerts but thresholds were too loose).

alex: oncall handoff: I'm oncall for next 2 hours, then Jordan will take remainder. I will update #oncall-handoff when I hand over.

deploy-bot: deploy runtime-deploy-20260314-73b2 completed at 14:29 UTC (rollback).

sam: verifying warmup strategy: we should replay hot request prefixes through an internal warmup endpoint instead of brute copying for TTL accuracy. Example curl script to warm top-k prefixes:
```
for id in $(cat top_prefixes.txt); do curl -s -X POST "https://internal.rewarm/v1?prefix=$id" &
done
wait
```

jordan: rekey job + warmup plan OK. I'll own running rekey job off-hours with rate limits and SRE oversight.

ira: customer update draft: "We detected increased latency between 14:20-14:35 UTC due to an internal key-format change that briefly caused cache misses; rollback completed and service restored. We're implementing compatibility guards and migration tooling to prevent recurrence." Approving now.

alex: great. Next: postmortem checklist items and owners:
- Root cause writeup (alex)
- CI guard for key schema (maria)
- Compatibility read-path PR + feature flag (sam)
- Rekey job + schedule (jordan)
- Add runbook threshold changes (maria)
- Customer follow-up (ira)

maria: assigning Jira INC-7123 for the postmortem and followups.

alex: last notes: we should add a code comment in key generation explaining that any change must include a migration plan, and require an entry in the deploy checklist. Also consider a small integration test that fails if key format changes without migration flag.

sam: +1. I'll bundle the compatibility read-path and a test to CI.

jordan: I'll run a small rekey dry-run on staging tonight and send results here.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: p99 returned to baseline within 4 minutes after rollback. Severity: Sev3 (customer impact limited, short duration). Postmortem owner: alex.

alex: handing off oncall to jordan now — see #oncall-handoff. I will start the postmortem draft and link it here when ready. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

jordan: taking over oncall. I will watch the rekey run and redis metrics. If anything spikes I'll escalate.

ira: closing customer comms loop: banner + emails sent, CS will follow up tomorrow with impacted accounts summary.

maria: logging final action items in INC-7123.

alex: end of thread.
